XSS is prevented (no live

minor.issue: Sanitiser strips only the tag markup, not the inner content between opening/closing tags. Input '<script>evil</script>testo' becomes 'eviltesto' (not 'testo' as claimed in the review request). This is XSS-safe because the surrounding esc() escapes any remaining special characters, but the AI's inner tag content leaks as visible text. Consider stripping <script>/<style>/<iframe> tag BODIES entirely for a stricter guarantee. Applies to both backend and frontend sanitisers (they share the same regex pattern).

action_items: OPTIONAL (hardening, not blocking): tighten the sanitiser to also drop the BODY of <script>/<style>/<iframe> tags — currently only the opening/closing tags are stripped and the inner text survives (e.g. '<script>alert(1)</script>testo' → 'alert(1)testo'). Not an XSS vector because esc() wraps the output, but visually ugly if AI ever emits such payloads. Applies to _sanitize_ai in /app/backend/server.py (~line 4133) and to sanitizeAi/sanitizeAiText in /app/frontend/src/BillsSection.tsx (~line 350) and /app/frontend/src/BillFieldRenderers.tsx (~line 27).

critical_code_review_comments: _sanitize_ai is defined LOCALLY inside _build_analysis_html and duplicated verbatim in two frontend files. Consider extracting to a single top-level helper (server: module-level function; frontend: single shared util imported by both files) so future edits stay in sync.
Frontend BillsSection.tsx is 2637 lines — well over the 700-line guideline. Recommend splitting into feature-specific sub-modules.

rca_of_issue:
Original bug — the AI (Claude Sonnet 5) sometimes returned text fields containing HTML tags (`
`, `

`) as markdown-like formatting. That text was then passed through html.escape()/escHtml() before being interpolated into the analysis HTML template, so `
` became `<br>` and rendered visibly to the user. The fix adds a sanitiser that strips ALL tags (`<[^>]+>` regex) but first converts semantic tags to newlines/bullets so the intent is preserved.
